I am an older man with some schooling, and I have been farming sorghum in the North West for many years. The rains are short here, so I know sorghum does better if I give it some strength with fertilizer—nothing too much, just enough to help it through the dry spells. I keep my own seed from last year's harvest because it is trusted and I do not need to spend money at the agro-dealer. My sons and I will work this small plot ourselves; there is no need to pay laborers for just this piece, and we have no pump or river nearby for watering.
